messages:
Megan: Heads-up: noticed ~12% tail-latency regression on 8xA100 nightly after kernel-selector change (selector v2 -> v2.1).
Samir: Can you paste the perf trace? Which workloads?
Megan: seq len 1024, batch 16, tp=1, pp=1, KV cache warm. Repro on commit abc123.
Kai: I'm seeing more allreduce stalls in the tracer. CC: @Ana
Ana: If it's scheduler drift, channel packing might be sending too many small collectives. Can you dump NCCLTRACE?
Megan: Attaching short snippet: ```LOG 12:03:45 allreduce start gid=42 size=128KB wait=1.2ms compute=0.8ms allreduce=4.5ms```
Jonah: Interesting — allreduce increased from ~2.1ms to ~4.5ms after change. Did selector switch to LL vs LL128?
Samir: Kernel selector diff toggled prefer_ll128=false for int8 kernels. Could fall back to algo=PROTO in some cases. I suspect channel count changed.
Megan: Run I did: ```./bench --gpus 8 --model gpt-large --seq 1024 --batch 16 --profile=ncdump``` Results show more serialized collectives.
Kai: Also saw KV cache prefetch to other ranks causing extra synchronization. Maybe prefetch ordering + smaller batches made more small allreduces.
Ana: Can you capture cgroups/netrank mapping? NCCL channel mapping depends on PCI topology; selector change might have changed buffer sizes that prevent LL128 pipelining.
Megan: Here's simple perf flame: `compute overlap plummeted from 65% -> 28%`
Jonah: Repro script to gather traces: ```export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; python tools/run_profile.py --trace nccl --out /tmp/trace```
Samir: :thumbsup: I'll run that on my rig. If we confirm channel count dropped, quick rollback to prefer_ll128=true should restore.
Kai: Flagging flaky nightly, bumped severity to P1 in the runbook. @infra-bot, create incident stub?
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-112, linked to nightly-run-8gpu.
Ana: If rollback fixes, we should add unit test for kernel selector that asserts combined allreduce time doesn't exceed baseline by >10% for standard configs.
Megan: Agreed. I'll attach traces to the incident. For context: selector change aimed to prefer smaller kernels to increase single-GPU throughput, clearly regressed multi-GPU overlap.
Jonah: Also consider adding microbench that runs with warm KV cache vs cold to catch prefetch-serialization interactions.
Samir: Running now, will paste logs in 30m.
Megan: :thanks:
